title: Transport Management and Freight Exchange Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Companies that compete for the same customers and jobs as a European transport-SaaS-plus-network business modeled on Alpega Group: enterprise shipper spend on TMS, freight procurement, and connected execution; carrier and forwarder membership in European spot freight exchanges; and the real-time visibility attach that sits on top of execution.
inclusionLogic: transport-management and network platforms that combine shipper software with a large connected carrier network
enterprise application suites whose TMS modules compete head-to-head in shipper RFPs for planning, procurement, and settlement
European road freight exchanges competing directly with Teleroute, Wtransnet, and Bursa Transport for spot-market liquidity
real-time transportation visibility platforms competing for the tracking and ETA layer of the shipper stack
digital road freight operators whose carrier network and shipper relationships substitute for exchange-based spot procurement in Europe
notes: Business stats are only included when they were found in official investor relations pages, official company or product pages, or official press releases; each stat preserves the company's reported scope.

Suite vendors (SAP, Oracle) report company-wide financials, not TMS-only figures; those metrics are labeled with company scope and included to show the scale asymmetry Alpega faces in enterprise deals.
US-only load boards (e.g. DAT) are excluded because they do not compete for European spot freight liquidity.

players.name: Transporeon (Trimble)
players.description: Transporeon is the closest structural competitor to an Alpega-style business: a European-origin transportation management platform that connects shippers and retailers to a very large carrier network for assignment, dock scheduling, visibility, and freight settlement. Acquired by Trimble in 2023, it now sits inside a global positioning-and-logistics technology group, giving it deep telematics reach and enterprise sales muscle in exactly the accounts Alpega targets.

players.name: SAP Transportation Management
players.description: SAP Transportation Management is the default TMS candidate in every European enterprise account that runs SAP ERP — which is most of Alpega's target shipper base. It competes on suite integration (order-to-cash, settlement, S/4HANA master data) rather than on a carrier network, and it is the incumbent Alpega most often has to displace or coexist with in planning and settlement.

players.name: Oracle Transportation Management
players.description: Oracle Transportation Management (OTM) is a long-standing leader-quadrant enterprise TMS with deep multi-mode optimization, global trade management adjacency, and a large installed base among multinationals. Like SAP, it competes on suite depth and optimization breadth rather than a connected European carrier network, and it anchors many of the RFPs where Alpega TMS is positioned as the more configurable European challenger.

players.name: Blue Yonder
players.description: Blue Yonder (a Panasonic group company) sells an end-to-end supply chain suite in which transportation management is bundled with demand planning, warehouse management, and order management. It competes for the same retail, manufacturing, and logistics-service-provider accounts as Alpega, typically leading with AI-driven planning breadth across the whole supply chain rather than road-freight network liquidity.

players.name: e2open (incl. BluJay)
players.description: e2open combines a multi-enterprise supply chain network with the BluJay transportation management assets it acquired in 2021, giving it a TMS-plus-network story that overlaps directly with Alpega's shipper products in Europe. Acquired by WiseTech Global in 2025, it is being folded into a global logistics-execution software group, which changes its roadmap but keeps it firmly in the same enterprise logistics deals.

players.name: Descartes Systems Group
players.description: Descartes operates the Global Logistics Network plus a broad, acquisition-built portfolio spanning routing, transportation management, customs and compliance, and e-commerce logistics. In Europe it competes with Alpega both in shipper TMS evaluations and in carrier-connectivity/EDI messaging, and its highly profitable network-plus-software model is the closest public-market comparable for a transport network business.

players.name: TIMOCOM
players.description: TIMOCOM operates Europe's largest road freight marketplace by daily offer volume and is the most direct competitor to the Teleroute/Wtransnet/Bursa Transport exchanges for carrier memberships and spot-market liquidity. Its strength is raw liquidity and reach across Western and Central Europe, extended with tracking, quote requests, and interfaces that push it from pure exchange toward a transaction platform.

players.name: Trans.eu Group
players.description: Trans.eu runs one of Europe's leading freight exchanges with particular depth in Poland and Central and Eastern Europe — the same carrier geography that powers much of the pan-European spot market. It has evolved from a classic open exchange into a platform with private exchanges, algorithmic freight matching, and shipper tools, competing directly with Bursa Transport and Teleroute for CEE liquidity.

players.name: Shippeo
players.description: Shippeo is the European leader in real-time multimodal transportation visibility, born in road freight and strong with exactly the continental European shippers Alpega serves. It competes for the visibility and predictive-ETA layer that Alpega bundles into execution, and its carrier-integration network makes it both a rival and an occasional ecosystem partner in shipper stacks.

players.name: project44
players.description: project44 is the largest global real-time visibility platform, tracking shipments across road, ocean, air, and rail for over a thousand enterprise brands. In Europe it competes with Shippeo — and with Alpega's own visibility and ETA products — for the tracking layer of enterprise transport stacks, and its scale in carriers, facilities, and data volume sets the benchmark for the category.

players.name: sennder
players.description: sennder is Europe's leading digital road freight operator: unlike Alpega it takes a principal position on loads, buying enterprise shipper freight and covering it with a contracted carrier network run on its sennOS platform. It competes with the freight exchanges for carrier attention and with the execution products for enterprise spot and contract freight, and its 2024 acquisition of C.H. Robinson's European Surface Transportation business made it a top-5 European FTL player.
